candidates.exact_span: monthly average of 20 mg/l and daily maximum of 30 mg/l
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes enforceable numeric TSS effluent limits (monthly average and daily maximum) that govern whether reported TSS measurements exceed applicable limits.

candidates.exact_span: effluent limitations for TSS are established in the draft permit identical to the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Determines whether FY2025 compliance comparisons use newly established limits or carry forward prior-permit numeric limits; a different reading of 'identical' or 'draft permit' could change which limit values apply.

candidates.exact_span: Loading limits are not established since the discharge is not a continuous one and is discharged from a holding lagoon on an as needed basis. This is identical to the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: For A, excludes mass-loading limits from enforceable numeric comparisons. For B, ties monitoring applicability to intermittent, as-needed discharge from a holding lagoon rather than continuous discharge. For C, documents a permit basis for periods without discharge or without loading-limit comparisons, affecting how missing or non-continuous results are classified.

candidates.exact_span: Water quality-based requirements are necessary where effluent limits more stringent than technology-based limits are necessary to maintain or achieve federal or state water quality limits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Frames when water-quality-based effluent limits may supplement or override technology-based limits; different interpretation of necessity could change which numeric limits are applicable for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: the low (0.177 MGD) volume of discharges
candidates.computation_change_reason: States discharge flow volume used in dilution and downstream-effects analysis; a different reading of this volume could change whether additional water-quality-based numeric limits are triggered or which dilution assumptions apply.

candidates.exact_span: less than approximately 0.064% of the flow in the San Juan River as it enters the Navajo Nation waters
candidates.computation_change_reason: Provides the dilution ratio relied on in downstream water-quality analysis; interpreting the percentage differently could change whether more stringent effluent limits beyond the stated TSS values are deemed applicable.

candidates.exact_span: the water quality standards of the Navajo Nation will not be affected
candidates.computation_change_reason: Concludes downstream tribal WQS are not implicated; if read as eliminating need for additional limits versus merely descriptive, it could change whether enforceable WQBELs beyond the stated TSS limits apply.

candidates.exact_span: Where these technology-based permit limits do not protect water quality or the designated uses, additional water quality-based effluent limitations and/or conditions are included in the NPDES permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets the trigger for imposing supplemental WQBELs; different interpretation of whether TBELs adequately protect designated uses could change which numeric limits are in force for compliance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: The discharge from the facility may enter Lower Animas Ditch / Hampton Arroyo and/or Williams Arroyo in Water body
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies receiving water bodies whose standards may govern applicable limits; uncertainty about which route(s) apply could change which state WQS and numeric limits are selected for comparison.
